title: Muse closes the gap
series: Branding and AI — how Muse would do the assignments

beats.line: A gap analysis is not a confession and not a plan. It's a table with three columns: what they ask for, what you have, and what you'll build. Here's how to fill it in — honestly.
beats.screen: Empty 3-column table: they ask / I have / to build.

beats.line: Four terms. Gap: what the posting wants that the résumé doesn't have. Evidence: proof, not adjectives. Build: the thing you'll make to close it. Link: the row where you already have it — don't rebuild, just link.
beats.screen: Four terms: gap / evidence / build / link.

beats.line: Start from Part 1's honest findings. Gap one: deep, hands-on Figma design-systems expertise — never shipped a design system in Figma. Gap two: public speaking at meetups and conferences. Gap three: travel up to twenty-five percent. All three were on the page in Part 1, so none of them are surprises.

Then add the second column. The seven-board sweep found Webflow's Senior Developer Educator — US remote, on camera — so the gap analysis now compares two postings, not one. A gap against one company is an anecdote; against two, it's a pattern.
beats.screen: Table gains a second column: Figma vs Webflow.

beats.line: Row one: written, visual, and video teaching material about the product. Have: hundreds of course videos, the deep-explainer pipeline, a Coursera MOOC. To build: tutorials about their product — Figma design systems plus MCP, a Webflow University-style build-along, a Notion API walkthrough. The skill transfers; the subject doesn't.
beats.screen: Row 1: teaching material about the product.

beats.line: Row two: on camera, in your own voice. Writer says so explicitly; Webflow says present on camera. Have: lecture recordings, studio work. To build: one three-to-five-minute on-camera sample — no synthetic narrator — teaching a single design-system idea. The voice has to be yours because the job says so.

Row three: hands-on depth in the tool. Figma design systems, tokens, Dev Mode; Webflow production sites. Have: Figma boards in class, a master's in information design. To build: one shipped Figma design system with tokens and a Dev Mode handoff, plus one production Webflow site — both open, both real. This is the biggest row, and it gets its own project.

Row four: community and public speaking. Have: a hundred fifty plus Fellows, an AI bootcamp for five hundred plus, conference talks. To build: a speaking reel cut from existing recordings, and a list of talks given. The evidence exists; it just needs editing.

Row five: comfort with AI-assisted workflows, MCP, evals. Have: the Prompt Engineering and Computational Skepticism courses, twenty-five plus deployed course bots. To build: nothing. Already covered — link, don't rebuild. Knowing which rows need no work is part of the analysis.

The build list, then — four things to make. Tutorials about their products. One on-camera sample. One shipped design system and one production site. One speaking reel. Each one maps to a row; each row maps to a posting requirement. Nothing on the list is decorative.
beats.screen: The build list: four things to make.

beats.line: And the biggest gap already has its project: the Madison project exists to close the Figma design-systems gap. That was stated in Part 1, before any building started. The course project isn't separate from the job search — it is the job search, with a syllabus.
beats.screen: Madison project card closing the Figma gap.

beats.line: The honest column stays public. This table lives in the repo, gaps and all — because a gap analysis you hide is just a résumé with extra steps. Gaps close by building, in the open, where the next posting can check your work.
beats.screen: The table stays public; gaps close by building.

beats.line: So: act one, name the gap — three honest findings, then a second column to compare against. Act two, the five rows — what they ask, what you have, what you'll build, including the row that needs nothing. Act three, the build list — four things to make, and the Madison project closing the biggest gap. Act four, the honest column — the table stays public.
beats.screen: Four recap lines, one per act.

beats.line: Your turn. Draw the three columns. Fill every row from real postings. And find the one row that says link, don't rebuild — it's the easiest win on the page.
beats.screen: Do-today card: draw the table; find the free row.

beats.line: Muse, in for Bear. Thanks for watching.
